title: React InstantSearch + Expo SDK 54 — TypeError: constructor is not callable
body: ### 🐛 Current behavior **### Description** After upgrading our app to Expo SDK 54, rendering results in a runtime error: `TypeError: constructor is not callable` The error occurs inside useInstantSearchApi when it executes: `var search = new InstantSearch(props);` So at runtime, the InstantSearch constructor from instantsearch.js is not callable. This worked correctly before upgrading Expo. ⸻ **### Environment** • Expo SDK: 54 • React Native: 0.81.5 • Hermes: enabled • react-instantsearch-core: 7.26.0 • instantsearch.js: 4.90.0 • Platform: iOS (simulator & device) • Bundler: Metro (default Expo config) ⸻ **### What changed** We upgraded from a previous Expo SDK version to SDK 54. No major changes were made to our InstantSearch setup. After the upgrade, the error occurs immediately when renders. ⸻ **### Error Location** Stack trace points to: ``` useInstantSearchApi.js (line 40) new InstantSearch(props) Component stack: ... ``` ⸻ **### Questions** 1. Is there a recommended configuration for using React InstantSearch with Expo SDK 54? Should we prefer a specific build (CJS vs ESM)? Any required Metro resolver settings? 2. Are there known compatibility notes with: Reanimated 4 react-native-worklets Expo 54 specifically? 3. Is instantsearch.js expected to work in a React Native + Expo environment, or is additional configuration required after recent SDK changes? ⸻ **### Additional Context** The error suggests the imported InstantSearch may not be the expected class at runtime (possibly due to ESM/CJS interop or Metro resolution changes in Expo 54). If needed, we can provide a minimal reproduction repository. ### 🔍 Steps to reproduce 1. Create a new Expo app using Expo SDK 54 `npx create-expo-app@latest` (ensure SDK 54 is used) 2. Install dependencies: `yarn add react-instantsearch-core instantsearch.js` 3. Enable Hermes (default in Expo 54). 4. Add a minimal setup: ``` import React from 'react'; import { InstantSearch } from 'react-instantsearch-core'; import InstantSearchJS from 'instantsearch.js'; export default function App() { return ( {/* minimal child */} ); } ``` 5. Run the app: `npx expo start` 6. Navigate to the screen rendering . ⸻ ### Actual Behavior The app crashes with: `TypeError: constructor is not callable` The error originates from: `new InstantSearch(props)` inside useInstantSearchApi. Add: console.log(typeof InstantSearch, InstantSearch); right before it’s instantiated. If it logs: • "object" instead of "function" → it’s an ESM interop issue. • undefined → Metro resolution issue. That will immediately narrow this down. If you show me your import statement, we can likely fix it today without waiting on GitHub. ### Live reproduction we don't have it ### 💭 Expected behavior ### Expected Behavior renders normally without runtime errors. ### Package version "react-instantsearch-core": "^7.26.0", "algoliasearch": "^5.49.1" ### Operating system iOS devices and Android Devices ### Browser Mobile apps ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

comments.body: Has this happened with previous versions too, or only one? do you have a reproduction somewhere we can see?

This was working fine 'till we upgrade the Expo's version to the 54. Unfortunately we can’t share a public reproduction repo (company code + environment constraints)
@Haroenv Do you have any guide on how to set InstantSearch's dependencies in an Expo project with the latests Expo SDK version?
There's no specific difference for Expo than for any other framework
@Haroenv  As requested, we’ve created a minimal reproduction repository to isolate the issue, without exposing our main codebase: https://github.com/devMozo/expo-algolia-poc
Yes, you're right, in CJS this line should be `var search = new InstantSearch.default(props);`. I'm looking if this recently changed

Yes, this did change, in the mean time, please use 7.25.0, the error was introduced in 7.26.0 with #6886 (see https://npmdiff.dev/react-instantsearch-core/7.25.0/7.26.0/package/dist/cjs/lib/useInstantSearchApi.js/)
